key_insight: Infrastructure as Code enabled deployment of a hospital-governed clinical AI service in about five minutes on average.
clinical_relevance: Browser-based access could simplify clinical AI integration, while an LLM checker flagged potentially severe inconsistencies in physician-approved documents.
method: Encoded backend infrastructure, private AI endpoints, and access controls as machine-readable configurations.
Measured deployment time across 25 runs at a tertiary care center.
Evaluated an LLM inconsistency checker on 1,347 documents with a severity-stratified physician audit.
evidence_signal: Deployment averaged 310.3 ± 196.6 seconds; severe inconsistencies were flagged in 105/1,347 documents (7.8%), and 149/150 audited findings were confirmed (population-weighted PPV 98.2%; CI 94.8–100.0).
watch_item: This single-center case study does not establish sensitivity for missed inconsistencies or improvements in patient outcomes.
paper_title: Introducing Infrastructure as Code for deployment and governance of medical AI: A case study
